tagline: Driving the evolution of connected commerce
hero_kpi_rationale: Recurring revenue is the primary driver of DBD's transformation toward a software and services model for banking and retail distributors, offering high margin and predictability.

kpis.name: Recurring / subscription revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from maintenance, software, and recurring service contracts.
kpis.description: DBD is gradually shifting its business model toward recurring revenue through service and software subscription contracts.
kpis.signal: Stable growth in the recurring model, key to the transformation.

kpis.name: Gross margin
kpis.explanation: Consolidated gross margin, reflecting profitability of activities after cost of sales.
kpis.description: Gross margin is slightly improving, driven by the growing share of higher-margin services.
kpis.signal: Improvement due to the shift toward higher-value services.

kpis.name: Operating margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin remains modest but is progressing, despite margin pressures on product lines.
kpis.signal: Slight improvement due to cost discipline.

kpis.name: R&D investments (% of revenue)
kpis.explanation: Research and development expenses as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: DBD invests modestly in R&D, focused on software solutions for distributors.
kpis.signal: R&D targeted on connected commerce software.

kpis.name: Capital expenditures (tangible and intangible assets)
kpis.explanation: Spending on tangible and intangible assets to maintain and expand operations.
kpis.description: Capex is contained, with a focus on efficiency rather than heavy expansion.
kpis.signal: Reduced capex, reflecting a priority on profitability.

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.description: DBD continues cost rationalization through headcount reduction.
kpis.signal: Ongoing headcount reduction to improve productivity.

kpis.name: Total revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Revenue of $3.806 Bn in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Net income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of $0.095 Bn in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: AI API call volume
kpis.explanation: Number of calls to artificial intelligence APIs in software solutions.
kpis.description: DBD is gradually integrating AI features into its service platforms, with rapid adoption.
kpis.signal: Explosive growth in AI adoption across customer services.

kpis.name: Percentage of deals including AI features
kpis.explanation: Percentage of new cloud contracts that include artificial intelligence capabilities.
kpis.description: The share of cloud deals including AI is rising rapidly, reflecting growing customer demand.
kpis.signal: AI increasingly embedded in cloud offerings.

risks.title: Cybersecurity risks
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions cybersecurity in the index (Item 1C), and the language used in these sections is generally strong to emphasize the importance of data and system protection. This risk is fundamental for a technology company.

risks.title: Competition risks in the IT market
risks.score_rationale: The information technology sector is inherently competitive. The intensity of language in the risk factors, even without specific excerpts, reflects constant pressure from competitors. This risk is major in this sector.

risks.title: Litigation and legal proceedings risks
risks.score_rationale: The presence of Item 3 'Legal Proceedings' with significant page numbers indicates that litigation is a notable concern. The language used in these sections is often cautious and highlights potential financial uncertainties.

risks.title: Risks related to rapid technological change
risks.score_rationale: As a technology company, the inability to keep pace with rapid innovation is an existential risk. The language used in technology risk factors is often strong to emphasize the need for constant adaptation.

risks.title: Supplier dependency risks
risks.score_rationale: Technology companies often rely on complex supply chains. Disruptions from key suppliers, even if not explicitly detailed here, represent a significant industry risk, often highlighted by cautious language.

risks.title: Regulatory compliance risks
risks.score_rationale: Technology companies operate in a complex and evolving regulatory environment (e.g., data protection). Failure to comply with regulations can result in fines and reputational damage, justifying a medium to high severity risk.

ai_positioning.summary: DBD does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing. There is no indication of AI use or development within the company.
